ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَهِّلِ الْكَافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْدًا (١٧)).
(رُوَيْدًا): a naʿt (adjective) for an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «إِمْهَالًا رُوَيْدًا» (a gentle respite); and «رُوَيْدًا» is the diminutive of «رُودٍ».
It is also said that it is a maṣdar with the augment omitted, the original being «إِرْوَادًا». [Translator's note: the printed text reads «مَصْدَرٌ مَحْذُوفٌ، الزِّيَادَةُ», apparently for «مَصْدَرٌ مَحْذُوفُ الزِّيَادَةِ»; translated accordingly.] And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خُلِقَ مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ (٦)).
(دَافِقٍ): it is by way of attribution (nasab), i.e. «ذُو انْدِفَاقٍ» (possessing gushing). It is also said that it is in the sense of «مَدْفُوقٍ» (poured forth).
It is also said that it is according to the meaning, because «انْدَفَقَ الْمَاءُ» (the water gushed) is in the sense of «نَزَلَ» (it came down).

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّهُ عَلَى رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ (٨) يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ (٩)).
The hāʾ in «رَجْعِهِ» refers back to man, so the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object; i.e. Allah is able to resurrect him. On this view, there are several aspects regarding the words of the Exalted «يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ»: the first is that it is governed by «قَادِرٌ». The second is that it is by way of clarification (tabyīn), i.e. «يَرْجِعُ يَوْمَ تُبْلَى» (he returns on the day [secrets] are tested). The third is that its implied form is «اذْكُرْ» (remember). It is not permissible that «رَجْعِهِ» govern it, because of the separation between them by the khabar (predicate).
It is also said that the hāʾ in «رَجْعِهِ» is for the water; i.e. able to return the water into the urethra or into the loins. On this view it is cut off from the words of the Exalted «يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ», and «اذْكُرْ» (remember) governs it.
